_comment: midnight - cool periwinkle icons to match the deep blue network editor.
The mechanism is `tint`, which keeps each pixel's own luminance and takes
only its hue from the theme. That matters for icons specifically: the
anti-aliasing and the inner shading of a glyph are luminance structure,
so a tint keeps them and a `solid` op would flatten them away.
What a tint can reach, because it is a fact about the shipped set rather
than about this theme: of the 97 icons, 69 are pure white with alpha and
25 are genuinely coloured, and both of those have luminance to preserve, so
the general op moves 94 of them. The remaining 3 - Cook, Grid and
CommentOffSmall - are pure black with alpha. There is no hue in a black
pixel to replace, so `tint` leaves them alone, and that is the right
outcome rather than a gap: they are dark ink drawn on a light tile, and
recolouring them would break the field they are meant to sit on.
The result is also brighter than the shipped icons on purpose. On this
theme's near-black worksheet, stock icons sit at roughly the same value as
the background and read as smudges.
Ops apply in order, and a later op wins, so the semantic groups below are
painted back over the general tint. Errors stay red and warnings stay
amber because a red error badge is a warning *to the operator*; recolouring
it to match the theme would remove the signal along with the hue.
